intro: In a debate, a public meeting or a tough team discussion, having an opinion isn't enough: you need an argument that holds up, an answer for the other side, and a reply when someone challenges you without warning. In this lesson you'll build and rebut arguments, think on your feet, and concede a point before you counter it. Warm-up: should your company try a four-day week?
teachingNotes: This speaking lesson builds on b2-discussion (buying time with That's a good question / Let me think, building on others, pros and cons, polite disagreement with I see what you mean, but …, I agree not *I am agree) and c1-hedging (a claim should match its evidence: suggests, not proves; tend to; one hedge is enough). Recap both in a line, don't re-teach them. Contexts: a university debate competition (the motion = the topic being debated, e.g. compulsory internships), a town-hall meeting about a new toll road near Bandung, and a team debate at a Jakarta startup about a four-day week. Keep facts general and safe; don't invent statistics about real organisations (a fictional faculty or office trial is fine).

Building and rebutting. A strong argument has four parts: claim (what you believe) → reason (why) → evidence or an example (facts, data, experience) → link back to the claim (So that's why …). This is like the PEEL paragraph some learners know from school; don't push the jargon. 'Everyone knows that …' is not evidence. Rebutting (membantah): That argument overlooks … (ignores something important), The evidence actually points the other way …, Even if that were true, … (were as in If I were you: imagining something you don't accept; 'was' is common in speech), That doesn't necessarily follow (the conclusion doesn't come automatically from the reason: belum tentu begitu). Attack the argument, never the person: *'You're too young to understand', *'You only say that because you live in Jakarta', *'That's a stupid idea' lose the audience and, in a debate competition, points.

Responding on the spot (respond-spontaneously). Buy time naturally, briefly: That's a good question. Let me put it this way … / What I'd say to that is … (a phrase to remember: don't analyse its structure) / It's a fair question, and the short answer is …. Ask for clarification when the challenge is unclear or exaggerated: Are you suggesting that …? / If I understand you correctly, you're saying that … (calm tone: 'Are you suggesting …?' can sound sharp if said angrily). Answer the question actually asked first (a number, yes/no, a direct answer), THEN explain, then bridge back to your point: Which brings me back to my main point … / And that's exactly why …. The typical fault is dodging: giving a prepared speech that doesn't answer the question. Audiences and judges notice.

Concede and counter (concede = admit the other side is partly right). Order: acknowledge first, then counter: That's a fair point, but … / I take your point; however, … / Granted, …, but … / I'd agree up to a point (= partly) / While it's true that …, … . Tone: concede sincerely and briefly, then counter calmly with a reason. Likely errors (the node lists none, so watch for these): *'I'm disagree' / *'I'm not agree' → I disagree / I don't agree (disagree is a verb); 'That's a fair point, but' used as an empty formula before ignoring the point → name the point (That's a fair point about the cost, but …) and vary the phrases; *'While it's true that the road is expensive, but it saves time' → no 'but' after a While / Although clause (Indonesian 'Walaupun …, tetapi …'); conceding without countering (That's a fair point, so I agree) when you still hold your view; rebutting the person instead of the argument.

Culture, presented respectfully: many Indonesians avoid open disagreement (sungkan, menjaga perasaan, especially with seniors), so they stay quiet or say 'Yes, maybe' while disagreeing; others open with a long polite preamble (Mohon maaf sebelumnya, dengan segala hormat, mungkin saya salah, tapi …), which in English delays and weakens the point; 'With all due respect' often comes right before strong disagreement and can sound irritated. The opposite habit is translating 'Itu salah' as a blunt 'That's wrong' / 'You are wrong'. In English debate the target is firm + polite: I see it differently, and here's why. / I disagree, because …. Disagreeing with an idea is normal and not a personal attack.

At C1 many choices are style: accept reasonable alternative phrases (I see your point / That's true, but / Admittedly / Although it's true that) and only mark clear faults (attacking the person, dodging the question, conceding without countering, 'While …, but …', I'm disagree). Grammar: A0–B2 plus hedging; no inversion, cleft sentences as a topic, subjunctive or impersonal passives. When the learner practises, play the opponent: make a claim or a sudden challenge, let them answer, react to the content first, then correct ONE thing.

keyPoints.title: Build an argument, then rebut the other side
keyPoints.explanation: A strong argument has four parts: a claim (what you believe), a reason (why), evidence or an example (facts, data, experience) and a link back (So that's why …). Match the claim to the evidence, as in the hedging lesson. To rebut, attack the argument, not the person: That argument overlooks … / The evidence actually points the other way … / Even if that were true, … / That doesn't necessarily follow. disagree is a verb: I disagree, not I'm disagree.

examples.en: That argument overlooks the fact that most residents here don't own a car.
examples.id: Argumen itu mengabaikan fakta bahwa sebagian besar warga di sini tidak punya mobil.

examples.en: Even if that were true, the road wouldn't solve the flooding problem.
examples.id: Seandainya itu pun benar, jalan itu tidak akan menyelesaikan masalah banjir.

examples.en: I disagree, and here's why: the trial only lasted two weeks.
examples.id: Saya tidak setuju, dan ini alasannya: uji cobanya hanya dua minggu.

id.title: Bangun argumen, lalu bantah argumen lawan
id.explanation: Argumen yang kuat punya empat bagian: klaim (apa yang kamu yakini), alasan (kenapa), bukti atau contoh (fakta, data, pengalaman) dan kembali ke klaim (So that's why …). Sesuaikan klaim dengan buktinya, seperti di pelajaran hedging. Untuk membantah, serang argumennya, bukan orangnya: That argument overlooks … / The evidence actually points the other way … / Even if that were true, … / That doesn't necessarily follow. disagree adalah kata kerja: I disagree, bukan I'm disagree.

keyPoints.title: Respond on the spot
keyPoints.explanation: When someone challenges you without warning: buy a moment naturally (That's a good question. Let me put it this way … / What I'd say to that is …), ask for clarification if the challenge is unclear (Are you suggesting that …? / If I understand you correctly, …), answer the question that was actually asked first, and then bridge back to your point (Which brings me back to my main point …). Don't dodge with a prepared speech.

examples.en: What I'd say to that is that the cost is only half of the story.
examples.id: Yang ingin saya sampaikan soal itu adalah biaya hanyalah separuh dari ceritanya.

examples.en: If I understand you correctly, you're saying the trial was too short.
examples.id: Kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, maksud Anda uji cobanya terlalu singkat.

examples.en: The short answer is no. And that's exactly why we need a proper study.
examples.id: Jawaban singkatnya tidak. Dan justru karena itulah kita butuh kajian yang serius.

id.title: Menanggapi secara spontan
id.explanation: Kalau seseorang menantangmu tanpa aba-aba: ulur waktu sebentar dengan wajar (That's a good question. Let me put it this way … / What I'd say to that is …), minta klarifikasi kalau tantangannya kurang jelas (Are you suggesting that …? / If I understand you correctly, …), jawab dulu pertanyaan yang benar-benar diajukan, lalu kembalikan ke poinmu (Which brings me back to my main point …). Jangan mengelak dengan pidato yang sudah kamu siapkan.

keyPoints.title: Concede a point, then counter it
keyPoints.explanation: To concede = to admit the other side is partly right. Acknowledge first, then counter with a reason: That's a fair point, but … / I take your point; however, … / Granted, …, but … / I'd agree up to a point / While it's true that …, … (no but after a While clause). Name the point you accept (That's a fair point about the cost, but …) so it doesn't sound like an empty formula, and vary the phrases.

examples.en: That's a fair point about the cost, but the road will save drivers an hour a day.
examples.id: Poin Anda soal biaya masuk akal, tapi jalan itu akan menghemat waktu pengendara satu jam sehari.

examples.en: Granted, a four-day week is hard to organise, but other startups have managed it.
examples.id: Memang benar, empat hari kerja seminggu sulit diatur, tapi startup lain berhasil melakukannya.

examples.en: I'd agree up to a point: the trial was short, but the results were clear.
examples.id: Saya setuju sampai batas tertentu: uji cobanya memang singkat, tapi hasilnya jelas.

id.title: Akui satu poin, lalu balas
id.explanation: To concede = mengakui bahwa pihak lain sebagian benar. Akui dulu, lalu balas dengan alasan: That's a fair point, but … / I take your point; however, … / Granted, …, but … / I'd agree up to a point / While it's true that …, … (tanpa but setelah anak kalimat While). Sebutkan poin yang kamu akui (That's a fair point about the cost, but …) supaya tidak terdengar seperti rumus kosong, dan variasikan frasanya.

guidedPractice.prompt: At a town-hall meeting, someone says: 'The road is brand new, so it must be safe.' Rebut the logic. Complete with one word: That doesn't necessarily ___. A new road can still have dangerous bends.
guidedPractice.hint: That doesn't necessarily follow = belum tentu begitu: the conclusion doesn't come automatically from the reason.

guidedPractice.prompt: A classmate says: 'Online classes are a waste of time.' You want to check what she really means. Complete with one word: Are you ___ that the university should stop all online classes?
guidedPractice.hint: Are you suggesting that …? = maksudmu …?: it checks the exact claim before you answer. Say it calmly.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word (= memang benar / harus diakui): ___, the train to Surabaya is slower, but it's much more comfortable than the bus.
guidedPractice.hint: Granted, … but … admits the other side's point first, then counters it.

guidedPractice.prompt: You accept your manager's point but still disagree. Complete with one word: I take your point; ___, a cheaper laptop won't last as long.
guidedPractice.hint: I take your point; however, … = saya paham poin Anda; namun, …: accept the point first, then counter it.

independentPractice.prompt: You don't accept your opponent's claim, but you want to show it wouldn't matter anyway. Complete with one word: Even if that ___ true, the road wouldn't solve the problem of flooding.
independentPractice.hint: Even if that were true = seandainya itu pun benar: were, as in If I were you (imagining). 'was' is also common in speech.

independentPractice.prompt: A journalist asks you a hard question. Buy a moment naturally. Complete with one word: That's a good question. Let me ___ it this way: the budget is fixed, but the timing isn't.
independentPractice.hint: Let me put it this way = begini …: it buys a second and introduces your answer.

independentPractice.prompt: Your opponent says the new parking building is badly needed. You have data that shows the opposite. Complete with one word: The evidence actually points the other ___: most of the spaces were empty last year.
independentPractice.hint: The evidence actually points the other way = buktinya justru menunjukkan sebaliknya.

assessment.prompt: At a town-hall meeting about a new toll road, Bu Ani argues: 'The toll road will hurt small businesses in our town (claim). Drivers will skip the town centre and stop buying food from local warung (reason). So the toll road is bad news for our town's economy (link back).' One part of a strong argument is missing. Which one? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: evidence (or an example): facts, data or experience that support the reason, e.g. what happened to shops in another town after a toll road opened. 'support' or 'statistics' = 90 (the right idea). 'reason', 'claim' or 'link back' = 0 (those three parts are already labelled in the argument).

assessment.prompt: At the same town-hall meeting, a speaker says the toll road will help everyone travel faster. Pak Hasan answers: 'That argument overlooks the fact that most people in our village don't own a car.' Which move is Pak Hasan making: concession, rebuttal or clarification? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: rebuttal (he shows a weakness in the other argument: it ignores people without cars). 'disagreement' or 'disagreeing' = 70 (true, but 'rebuttal' is the move from the list). 'concession' = 0 (he doesn't admit the other side is right). 'clarification' = 0 (he isn't asking what the speaker means).

assessment.prompt: In a team debate about a four-day week, Dimas wants to disagree firmly but politely. Correct the mistake in his sentence: I'm disagree with that argument.
acceptableAnswers: i don't agree with that argument
i do not agree with that argument
i don't agree with this argument
i do not agree with this argument
assessment.rubric: Correct: I disagree with that argument (disagree is a verb, so there's no am) or I don't agree with that argument. 'I'm not agree' = 20 (the same mistake: agree is a verb too). 'I am disagree' = 0. 'I disagree that argument' = 60 (no am, good, but disagree needs with). 'That's wrong' = 30 (no mistake fixed, and it sounds blunt).

assessment.prompt: In a university debate competition, the opposing speaker says students should do internships during the holidays. Sari stands up and asks: 'Are you suggesting that students should work for free every holiday?' Which move is Sari making: concession, rebuttal or clarification? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: clarification (Are you suggesting that …? checks exactly what the opponent means before she answers; in a debate it can also show that a claim goes too far). 'question' = 60 (true, but not the move from the list). 'rebuttal' = 30 (she hasn't argued against anything yet). 'concession' = 0.

assessment.prompt: In a university debate, an opponent suddenly asks Dimas how much compulsory internships would cost the faculty. He answers the question in two sentences and then returns to his own argument. Complete with one word: Which brings me ___ to my main point: internships help students find jobs faster.
assessment.rubric: Correct: back (Which brings me back to my main point = dan itu membawa saya kembali ke poin utama saya: a bridge after answering the question). 'again' = 30 (not the phrase). 'to' or 'into' = 0.

assessment.prompt: In a team debate at a startup in Jakarta, Sari says clients expect a reply on Fridays. You agree that this is a real problem, but you still support the four-day week. Complete with one word: I take your ___, but we could have a small team on duty every Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: point (I take your point = saya paham dan menerima poin Anda; then but … counters it). 'idea' = 50 (understandable but not the fixed phrase). 'view' or 'opinion' = 40 (I take your point is the phrase). 'side' = 20.

assessment.prompt: At the town-hall meeting, you accept one argument for the toll road but still oppose it. Complete with one word: ___ it's true that the new toll road will create jobs, most of those jobs will only last while it's being built.
assessment.rubric: Correct: While (While it's true that …, … = meskipun benar bahwa …, …: concede in the first part, counter in the second; no but after it). Whilst (British), Although, Though and Even though are also correct. 'Granted' = 50 (Granted, it's true that … needs a comma and but later). 'Because' or 'Since' = 0 (they give a reason, not a concession). 'But' = 0.

material.title: Building an argument that holds up

blocks.text:
Quick recap: from B2 you can buy time (*That's a good question*), build on others and disagree politely (*I see what you mean, but …*). From the hedging lesson you know that **a claim should match its evidence**. A debate asks for more: an argument that still stands when someone attacks it.

A strong argument has **four parts**:
- **Claim** (*klaim*): what you believe. *Our company should try a four-day week.*
- **Reason** (*alasan*): why. *People do better work when they're well rested.*
- **Evidence or an example** (*bukti atau contoh*): facts, data or real experience that support the reason. *When our Bandung office tried it for three months, sick days fell by a third.*
- **Link back** (*kembali ke klaim*): connect it to your claim again. *So that's why a four-day week makes sense for us.*

The part learners most often skip is **evidence**. *Everyone knows that …* or *It's obvious that …* is not evidence: it's just the claim said louder.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: dari B2 kamu sudah bisa mengulur waktu (*That's a good question*), melanjutkan poin orang lain dan tidak setuju dengan sopan (*I see what you mean, but …*). Dari pelajaran hedging kamu tahu bahwa **klaim harus sesuai dengan buktinya**. Debat menuntut lebih: argumen yang tetap berdiri walaupun diserang.

Argumen yang kuat punya **empat bagian**:
- **Claim** (*klaim*): apa yang kamu yakini. *Our company should try a four-day week.*
- **Reason** (*alasan*): kenapa. *People do better work when they're well rested.*
- **Evidence or an example** (*bukti atau contoh*): fakta, data atau pengalaman nyata yang mendukung alasannya. *When our Bandung office tried it for three months, sick days fell by a third.*
- **Link back** (*kembali ke klaim*): hubungkan lagi dengan klaimmu. *So that's why a four-day week makes sense for us.*

Bagian yang paling sering dilewati adalah **bukti**. *Everyone knows that …* atau *It's obvious that …* bukan bukti: itu cuma klaim yang diucapkan lebih keras.

rows.en: Students learn skills that lectures can't teach, like dealing with real clients.
rows.id: Mahasiswa belajar keterampilan yang tidak bisa diajarkan di kuliah, seperti menghadapi klien sungguhan.

rows.en: In our faculty, students who did an internship found their first job about four months sooner.
rows.id: Di fakultas kami, mahasiswa yang pernah magang mendapat pekerjaan pertama sekitar empat bulan lebih cepat.

rows.en: So that's why internships should be part of every degree.
rows.id: Jadi karena itulah magang sebaiknya menjadi bagian dari setiap program studi.

blocks.text: Your hedging skills matter here. If your evidence is one trial or one survey, don't claim too much: *The trial **suggests** that a four-day week **may** reduce sick days*, not *proves*. An opponent will attack a claim that's stronger than its evidence first, so a careful claim is harder to rebut.

id.text: Kemampuan hedging-mu berguna di sini. Kalau buktimu hanya satu uji coba atau satu survei, jangan mengklaim terlalu banyak: *The trial **suggests** that a four-day week **may** reduce sick days*, bukan *proves*. Lawan akan menyerang lebih dulu klaim yang lebih kuat daripada buktinya, jadi klaim yang hati-hati lebih sulit dibantah.

blocks.prompt: Budi claims: 'Our office should allow working from home two days a week.' Which sentence is EVIDENCE for his claim?
options: Working from home is clearly the future of work.
During last year's three-month trial, our team finished 15% more tasks on home days.
So that's why we should allow it.
blocks.explain: The trial result is **evidence**: real data from their own office. The first sentence is just another claim (and *clearly* is too strong without data). The third is the **link back**: useful at the end, but it doesn't prove anything.

id.prompt: Budi berpendapat: 'Our office should allow working from home two days a week.' Kalimat mana yang menjadi BUKTI untuk klaimnya?
id.explain: Hasil uji coba itu adalah **bukti**: data nyata dari kantor mereka sendiri. Kalimat pertama cuma klaim lain (dan *clearly* terlalu kuat tanpa data). Kalimat ketiga adalah **kembali ke klaim**: berguna di akhir, tapi tidak membuktikan apa pun.

material.title: Rebutting: attack the argument, not the person

blocks.text:
To **rebut** (*membantah*) means to show where the other side's argument is weak. Four useful moves:
- **That argument overlooks …** (*argumen itu mengabaikan …*): it ignores something important. *That argument overlooks the fact that most residents don't own a car.*
- **The evidence actually points the other way.** (*buktinya justru menunjukkan sebaliknya*): the data says the opposite.
- **Even if that were true, …** (*seandainya itu pun benar, …*): you don't accept the claim, but you show it wouldn't matter anyway. **were** here is the same as in *If I were you* (B1): you're imagining something. In everyday speech *was* is also common.
- **That doesn't necessarily follow.** (*belum tentu begitu*): the conclusion doesn't come automatically from the reason. *The road is new, so it must be safe?* That doesn't necessarily follow.

**Attack the argument, never the person.** These lose the audience (and, in a debate competition, points):
- ✗ *You're too young to understand the budget.*
- ✗ *You only say that because you live in Jakarta.*
- ✗ *That's a stupid idea.*
Instead, talk about the idea: *That plan overlooks the cost of maintenance.*

id.text:
**Rebut** (*membantah*) artinya menunjukkan di mana argumen pihak lain lemah. Empat langkah yang berguna:
- **That argument overlooks …** (*argumen itu mengabaikan …*): ada hal penting yang tidak diperhatikan. *That argument overlooks the fact that most residents don't own a car.*
- **The evidence actually points the other way.** (*buktinya justru menunjukkan sebaliknya*): datanya mengatakan hal yang berlawanan.
- **Even if that were true, …** (*seandainya itu pun benar, …*): kamu tidak menerima klaimnya, tapi kamu tunjukkan bahwa itu tetap tidak berpengaruh. **were** di sini sama seperti di *If I were you* (B1): kamu sedang membayangkan sesuatu. Dalam percakapan sehari-hari *was* juga umum.
- **That doesn't necessarily follow.** (*belum tentu begitu*): kesimpulannya tidak otomatis muncul dari alasannya. *The road is new, so it must be safe?* That doesn't necessarily follow.

**Serang argumennya, jangan pernah orangnya.** Kalimat seperti ini membuat penonton tidak simpati (dan di lomba debat, nilaimu berkurang):
- ✗ *You're too young to understand the budget.*
- ✗ *You only say that because you live in Jakarta.*
- ✗ *That's a stupid idea.*
Sebaliknya, bicarakan idenya: *That plan overlooks the cost of maintenance.*

rows.en: That argument overlooks the cost of maintaining the road for thirty years.
rows.id: Argumen itu mengabaikan biaya perawatan jalan selama tiga puluh tahun.
rows.note: shows what the other side ignored

id.note: menunjukkan apa yang diabaikan pihak lain

rows.en: The evidence actually points the other way: online sales grew while the shop was closed.
rows.id: Buktinya justru menunjukkan sebaliknya: penjualan online naik selama tokonya tutup.

rows.en: Even if that were true, it wouldn't justify closing the whole department.
rows.id: Seandainya itu pun benar, itu tidak cukup jadi alasan untuk menutup seluruh departemen.

rows.en: Fewer hours doesn't mean less work. That doesn't necessarily follow.
rows.id: Jam kerja lebih sedikit tidak berarti pekerjaan lebih sedikit. Belum tentu begitu.

blocks.text:
**Firm + polite: two Indonesian habits to adjust.** Many of us avoid open disagreement (*sungkan*, *menjaga perasaan*), especially with seniors, so we stay quiet or say *Yes, maybe* while we disagree. Others open with a long preamble (*Mohon maaf sebelumnya, dengan segala hormat, mungkin saya salah, tapi …*): in English it delays and weakens your point, and **With all due respect** often comes right before strong disagreement, so it can sound irritated. The opposite habit is translating *Itu salah!* as a blunt **That's wrong!** or **You are wrong!**, which sounds aggressive. In an English debate, disagreeing with an idea is normal, not a personal attack. Aim for firm and polite:
- ✓ *I see it differently, and here's why.*
- ✓ *I disagree, because …* (**disagree** is a verb: never *I'm disagree* or *I'm not agree*).

id.text:
**Tegas + sopan: dua kebiasaan orang Indonesia yang perlu disesuaikan.** Banyak dari kita menghindari ketidaksetujuan terbuka (*sungkan*, *menjaga perasaan*), apalagi dengan senior, jadi kita diam saja atau bilang *Yes, maybe* padahal tidak setuju. Ada juga yang membuka dengan pengantar panjang (*Mohon maaf sebelumnya, dengan segala hormat, mungkin saya salah, tapi …*): dalam bahasa Inggris ini menunda dan melemahkan poinmu, dan **With all due respect** sering muncul tepat sebelum ketidaksetujuan yang keras, jadi bisa terdengar kesal. Kebiasaan sebaliknya adalah menerjemahkan *Itu salah!* menjadi **That's wrong!** atau **You are wrong!** yang terdengar agresif. Dalam debat berbahasa Inggris, tidak setuju dengan sebuah ide itu biasa, bukan serangan pribadi. Usahakan tegas dan sopan:
- ✓ *I see it differently, and here's why.*
- ✓ *I disagree, because …* (**disagree** adalah kata kerja: jangan pernah *I'm disagree* atau *I'm not agree*).

blocks.prompt: In a team debate, Rina says: 'Our team is too small for a four-day week.' Which reply rebuts her argument, not her as a person?
options: You always say no to new ideas, Rina.
That argument overlooks the fact that two other teams of our size already work four days.
With all due respect, you are wrong.
blocks.explain: **That argument overlooks …** points to something Rina's argument ignores, with a fact. The first reply attacks Rina herself. The third is blunt (*you are wrong*) and gives no reason; *With all due respect* doesn't make it softer.

id.prompt: Dalam debat tim, Rina berkata: 'Our team is too small for a four-day week.' Balasan mana yang membantah argumennya, bukan Rina sebagai orang?
id.explain: **That argument overlooks …** menunjuk hal yang diabaikan argumen Rina, dengan fakta. Balasan pertama menyerang Rina sendiri. Balasan ketiga terlalu blak-blakan (*you are wrong*) dan tidak memberi alasan; *With all due respect* tidak membuatnya lebih halus.

blocks.text:
In a debate or a public meeting, the hardest moment is the sudden question. Four steps help:

**1. Buy a moment, briefly.** You know *That's a good question* and *Let me think* from B2. Add:
- **That's a good question. Let me put it this way …** (*pertanyaan bagus. Begini …*)
- **What I'd say to that is …** (*yang ingin saya sampaikan soal itu adalah …*): a phrase to remember as one piece.
- **It's a fair question, and the short answer is …** (*pertanyaan yang wajar, dan jawaban singkatnya …*)
One phrase is enough: then answer.

**2. Clarify if the challenge is unclear or exaggerated.**
- **Are you suggesting that …?** (*maksud Anda …?*)
- **If I understand you correctly, you're saying that …** (*kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, maksud Anda …*)
Say these calmly: in an angry voice, *Are you suggesting …?* sounds like an attack.

**3. Answer the question that was actually asked.** If they ask *how many* or *how much*, give the number first. Don't dodge with the speech you prepared: audiences and judges notice.

**4. Bridge back to your point.**
- **Which brings me back to my main point …** (*dan itu membawa saya kembali ke poin utama saya …*)
- **And that's exactly why …** (*dan justru karena itulah …*)

id.text:
Dalam debat atau pertemuan publik, momen tersulit adalah pertanyaan mendadak. Empat langkah ini membantu:

**1. Ulur waktu sebentar saja.** Kamu sudah tahu *That's a good question* dan *Let me think* dari B2. Tambahkan:
- **That's a good question. Let me put it this way …** (*pertanyaan bagus. Begini …*)
- **What I'd say to that is …** (*yang ingin saya sampaikan soal itu adalah …*): frasa yang diingat sebagai satu kesatuan.
- **It's a fair question, and the short answer is …** (*pertanyaan yang wajar, dan jawaban singkatnya …*)
Satu frasa sudah cukup: lalu jawab.

**2. Minta klarifikasi kalau tantangannya kurang jelas atau dilebih-lebihkan.**
- **Are you suggesting that …?** (*maksud Anda …?*)
- **If I understand you correctly, you're saying that …** (*kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, maksud Anda …*)
Ucapkan dengan tenang: dengan nada marah, *Are you suggesting …?* terdengar seperti serangan.

**3. Jawab pertanyaan yang benar-benar diajukan.** Kalau ditanya *how many* atau *how much*, sebutkan angkanya dulu. Jangan mengelak dengan pidato yang sudah kamu siapkan: penonton dan juri akan sadar.

**4. Kembalikan ke poinmu.**
- **Which brings me back to my main point …** (*dan itu membawa saya kembali ke poin utama saya …*)
- **And that's exactly why …** (*dan justru karena itulah …*)

rows.en: It's a fair question, and the short answer is about Rp 40 million a year.
rows.id: Pertanyaan yang wajar, dan jawaban singkatnya sekitar Rp 40 juta per tahun.

rows.en: If I understand you correctly, you're saying the plan is too expensive for small firms.
rows.id: Kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, maksud Anda rencana itu terlalu mahal untuk perusahaan kecil.

rows.en: And that's exactly why we need a three-month trial first.
rows.id: Dan justru karena itulah kita butuh uji coba tiga bulan dulu.

blocks.prompt: At a town-hall meeting, a resident shouts: 'So you want to destroy our village for a road!' You think he has misunderstood the plan. What's the best first reply?
options: Are you suggesting that the road will go through the village itself? Because the plan actually goes around it.
Calm down. You clearly haven't read the plan.
That's a good question. Let me think.
blocks.explain: **Are you suggesting that …?** checks the exaggerated claim calmly and then corrects it with a fact. The second reply attacks the person. The third doesn't fit: he didn't ask a question, and *Let me think* doesn't answer his worry.

id.prompt: Di sebuah pertemuan warga, seorang warga berteriak: 'So you want to destroy our village for a road!' Menurutmu dia salah paham soal rencananya. Apa balasan pertama yang terbaik?
id.explain: **Are you suggesting that …?** memeriksa klaim yang dilebih-lebihkan dengan tenang, lalu meluruskannya dengan fakta. Balasan kedua menyerang orangnya. Balasan ketiga tidak cocok: dia tidak bertanya, dan *Let me think* tidak menjawab kekhawatirannya.

blocks.text:
To **concede** (*mengakui*) means to admit that the other side is partly right. Strong speakers do it on purpose: it shows you're fair and listening, and it makes your counter-argument more believable. The order matters: **acknowledge first, then counter with a reason.**
- **That's a fair point, but …** (*poin yang masuk akal, tapi …*)
- **I take your point; however, …** (*saya paham dan menerima poin Anda; namun …*)
- **Granted, …, but …** (*memang benar …, tapi …*): *Granted, the road is expensive, but it will save drivers an hour a day.*
- **I'd agree up to a point.** (*saya setuju sampai batas tertentu*): you agree only partly.
- **While it's true that …, …** (*meskipun benar bahwa …, …*)

**Tone:** concede sincerely and briefly, then counter calmly. If you say *That's a fair point, but …* to every comment and then ignore the point, it sounds like an empty formula. **Name the point** you accept and vary the phrases: *That's a fair point **about the cost**, but …*.

And don't stop after the concession if you still hold your view: *That's a fair point, so I agree* gives the debate away.

id.text:
**Concede** (*mengakui*) artinya mengakui bahwa pihak lain sebagian benar. Pembicara yang kuat melakukannya dengan sengaja: ini menunjukkan kamu adil dan mendengarkan, dan membuat bantahanmu lebih meyakinkan. Urutannya penting: **akui dulu, lalu balas dengan alasan.**
- **That's a fair point, but …** (*poin yang masuk akal, tapi …*)
- **I take your point; however, …** (*saya paham dan menerima poin Anda; namun …*)
- **Granted, …, but …** (*memang benar …, tapi …*): *Granted, the road is expensive, but it will save drivers an hour a day.*
- **I'd agree up to a point.** (*saya setuju sampai batas tertentu*): kamu hanya setuju sebagian.
- **While it's true that …, …** (*meskipun benar bahwa …, …*)

**Nada:** akui dengan tulus dan singkat, lalu balas dengan tenang. Kalau kamu bilang *That's a fair point, but …* untuk setiap komentar lalu mengabaikan poinnya, itu terdengar seperti rumus kosong. **Sebutkan poin** yang kamu akui dan variasikan frasanya: *That's a fair point **about the cost**, but …*.

Dan jangan berhenti setelah mengakui kalau kamu masih memegang pendapatmu: *That's a fair point, so I agree* sama saja menyerahkan debatnya.

rows.en: That's a fair point about training costs, but most interns stay with the company afterwards.
rows.id: Poin soal biaya pelatihan itu masuk akal, tapi kebanyakan peserta magang tetap bekerja di perusahaan itu sesudahnya.

rows.en: I take your point; however, the delay will cost us more in the long run.
rows.id: Saya paham poin Anda; namun, penundaan itu akan merugikan kita lebih besar dalam jangka panjang.

rows.en: While it's true that the trial was short, the results were very consistent.
rows.id: Meskipun benar bahwa uji cobanya singkat, hasilnya sangat konsisten.
rows.note: no but in the second part

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: **Walaupun …, tetapi …** is normal in Indonesian, but in English a *While* / *Although* clause already shows the contrast, so **don't add but**.
- ✓ *While it's true that the road is expensive, it will save time.*
- ✗ *While it's true that the road is expensive, but it will save time.*
With **Granted, …** it's the other way round: you **do** need *but* later (*Granted, it's expensive, but …*).

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **Walaupun …, tetapi …** wajar dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris anak kalimat *While* / *Although* sudah menunjukkan kontras, jadi **jangan tambahkan but**.
- ✓ *While it's true that the road is expensive, it will save time.*
- ✗ *While it's true that the road is expensive, but it will save time.*
Dengan **Granted, …** justru sebaliknya: kamu **perlu** but di bagian berikutnya (*Granted, it's expensive, but …*).

blocks.prompt: Which sentence concedes a point and then counters it correctly?
options: While it's true that the office is small, but we can still fit a new team.
We can still fit a new team. The office is small, that's a fair point, so I agree.
Granted, the office is small, but we can still fit a new team if we share desks.
blocks.explain: **Granted, …, but …** admits the point first and then counters it with a reason (sharing desks). The first sentence has an extra *but* after a *While* clause. The second gives up: it ends by agreeing instead of countering.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang mengakui satu poin lalu membalasnya dengan benar?
id.explain: **Granted, …, but …** mengakui poinnya dulu, lalu membalas dengan alasan (berbagi meja). Kalimat pertama punya *but* tambahan setelah anak kalimat *While*. Kalimat kedua menyerah: berakhir dengan setuju, bukan membalas.

resources.title: How to disagree productively and find common ground | Julia Dhar
resources.note: A TED talk (about 15 minutes) by a former world debate champion: how to disagree well at work and at home, starting from common ground and separating the idea from the person. Natural, fast native-level English, so turn on the subtitles if you need them.

id.note: TED talk (sekitar 15 menit) oleh mantan juara debat dunia: cara tidak setuju dengan baik di kantor dan di rumah, mulai dari kesamaan pandangan dan memisahkan ide dari orangnya. Bahasa Inggrisnya alami dan cepat seperti penutur asli, jadi nyalakan subtitle kalau perlu.

resources.title: 20 Two-Word Expressions to Agree & Disagree in English
resources.note: An engVid lesson page (a video plus a quiz) on short replies for agreeing, disagreeing and conceding, such as fair enough, good point and I suppose. Marked intermediate to advanced, so some of it is review, but it's handy for quick, natural concessions.

id.note: Halaman pelajaran engVid (video plus kuis) tentang balasan pendek untuk setuju, tidak setuju dan mengakui poin, seperti fair enough, good point dan I suppose. Ditandai tingkat menengah sampai mahir, jadi sebagian berupa ulasan, tapi berguna untuk mengakui poin dengan cepat dan alami.

id.intro: Dalam debat, pertemuan publik atau diskusi tim yang alot, punya pendapat saja tidak cukup: kamu butuh argumen yang kokoh, jawaban untuk pihak lawan, dan tanggapan saat seseorang menantangmu tanpa aba-aba. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan membangun dan membantah argumen, berpikir cepat saat ditantang, dan mengakui satu poin sebelum membalasnya. Pemanasan: apakah perusahaanmu sebaiknya mencoba empat hari kerja seminggu?
suggestedQuestions: Bukankah tidak sopan kalau terang-terangan tidak setuju dengan orang yang lebih senior?
Apa yang sebaiknya saya katakan kalau saya tidak tahu jawaban dari sebuah tantangan?
Apakah 'That's a fair point, but…' selalu sopan?
Apa bedanya membantah argumen dan menyerang orangnya?

assessment.db-1: Di pertemuan warga tentang jalan tol baru, Bu Ani berargumen: 'The toll road will hurt small businesses in our town (claim). Drivers will skip the town centre and stop buying food from local warung (reason). So the toll road is bad news for our town's economy (link back).' Satu bagian dari argumen yang kuat tidak ada. Bagian yang mana? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.db-2: Di pertemuan warga yang sama, seorang pembicara bilang jalan tol itu akan membuat semua orang bepergian lebih cepat. Pak Hasan menjawab: 'That argument overlooks the fact that most people in our village don't own a car.' Langkah apa yang dilakukan Pak Hasan: concession, rebuttal atau clarification? Tulis satu kata.
assessment.db-3: Dalam debat tim tentang empat hari kerja seminggu, Dimas ingin tidak setuju dengan tegas tapi sopan. Perbaiki kesalahan dalam kalimatnya: I'm disagree with that argument.
assessment.db-4: Dalam lomba debat antaruniversitas, pembicara lawan bilang mahasiswa sebaiknya magang saat liburan. Sari berdiri dan bertanya: 'Are you suggesting that students should work for free every holiday?' Langkah apa yang dilakukan Sari: concession, rebuttal atau clarification? Tulis satu kata.
assessment.db-5: Dalam debat antaruniversitas, lawan tiba-tiba bertanya kepada Dimas berapa biaya magang wajib bagi fakultas. Dia menjawab pertanyaan itu dalam dua kalimat, lalu kembali ke argumennya sendiri. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Which brings me ___ to my main point: internships help students find jobs faster.
assessment.db-6: Dalam debat tim di sebuah startup di Jakarta, Sari bilang klien mengharapkan balasan pada hari Jumat. Kamu setuju bahwa ini masalah nyata, tapi kamu tetap mendukung empat hari kerja seminggu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I take your ___, but we could have a small team on duty every Friday.
assessment.db-7: Di pertemuan warga, kamu menerima satu argumen yang mendukung jalan tol, tapi kamu tetap menolaknya. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: ___ it's true that the new toll road will create jobs, most of those jobs will only last while it's being built.
